---
title: Multi Node
description: How to use Axolotl on multiple machines
---

The below are three ways to train multi-node in Axolotl.

::: {.callout-important}
Each machine needs a copy of Axolotl, we suggest using the same commit to ensure compatibility.

You will also need to have the same configuration file for your model on each machine.

Make sure the main machine is reachable by other machines.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
Launcher and cluster settings can live in a reusable [runtime config](runtime-config.qmd)
(`axolotl train config.yaml --runtime cluster.yaml`) instead of per-node
accelerate configs or long `--` passthrough strings. The runtime file contains
no machine ranks, so the identical file works on every node.
:::

## Ray (recommended)

Ray needs no rank bookkeeping at all: bring up a Ray cluster once (or let
`axolotl ray up --hostfile hostfile` do it over ssh), then launch from the head
node — or submit from anywhere with the Jobs API:

```yaml
# cluster.yaml
launcher: ray
ray:
  num_workers: auto  # every GPU in the cluster
  # address: http://head:8265   # to submit remotely via the Ray Jobs API
```

```bash
axolotl train config.yaml --runtime cluster.yaml
```

See the [Ray integration guide](ray-integration.qmd) for cluster setup, remote
job submission, and GPU-type constraints.

## Torchrun

If you are using Infiniband, we recommend torchrun to utilize the full bandwidth.

Set the following env (change buffersize/socketname depending on your system):

```bash
export NCCL_IB_DISABLE=0
export NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME="eth0,en,eth,em,bond"
export NCCL_BUFFSIZE=2097152
```

### Option 1: Runtime config (Recommended)

Write the rendezvous details once and run the same command on every node:

```yaml
# torchrun-cluster.yaml (identical on all nodes)
launcher: torchrun
torchrun:
  nnodes: 2
  nproc_per_node: 8
  rdzv_id: my-run
  rdzv_backend: c10d
  rdzv_endpoint: 10.0.0.4:29400
```

```bash
axolotl train config.yaml --runtime torchrun-cluster.yaml
```

### Option 2: Launcher args passthrough

```bash
axolotl train config.yaml --launcher torchrun -- --nnodes $num_nodes --nproc_per_node $gpu_per_node --rdzv_id $rdzv_id --rdzv_backend c10d --rdzv_endpoint "$head_node_ip:$head_node_port"
```

### Option 3: Direct torchrun (Legacy)

```bash
torchrun --nnodes $num_nodes --nproc_per_node $gpu_per_node --rdzv_id $rdzv_id --rdzv_backend c10d --rdzv_endpoint "$head_node_ip:$head_node_port" -m axolotl.cli.train config.yaml
```

Please make sure to substitute the placeholder variables:

- `num_nodes`: Number of nodes (containing GPUs)
- `gpu_per_node`: Number of gpus per node
- `head_node_ip`: IP of the head node (make sure other machines can connect to this)
- `head_node_port`: Port of the head node (make sure other machines can connect to this. Default 29400)
- `rdzv_id`: A unique job ID that is used by the job across nodes.

More info on the available configs can be found on the Pytorch docs [here](https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/elastic/run.html)

## Accelerate

You will need to create a configuration for accelerate, either by using `accelerate config` and follow the instructions or you can use one of the preset below:

~/.cache/huggingface/accelerate/default_config.yaml
```yaml
compute_environment: LOCAL_MACHINE
debug: false
distributed_type: FSDP
downcast_bf16: 'no'
machine_rank: 0 # Set to 0 for the main machine, increment by one for other machines
main_process_ip: 10.0.0.4 # Set to main machine's IP
main_process_port: 5000
main_training_function: main
mixed_precision: bf16
num_machines: 2 # Change to the number of machines
num_processes: 4 # That's the total number of GPUs, (for example: if you have 2 machines with 4 GPU, put 8)
rdzv_backend: static
same_network: true
tpu_env: []
tpu_use_cluster: false
tpu_use_sudo: false
use_cpu: false
```

Alternatively, keep the shared settings in a runtime config and pass only the
per-node rank on the command line:

```bash
# node 0
axolotl train config.yaml --runtime examples/runtime/accelerate-2node.yaml -- --machine_rank 0
# node 1
axolotl train config.yaml --runtime examples/runtime/accelerate-2node.yaml -- --machine_rank 1
```

Configure your model to use FSDP in the Axolotl yaml. For example:
```yaml
fsdp_version: 2
fsdp_config:
  offload_params: true
  state_dict_type: FULL_STATE_DICT
  auto_wrap_policy: TRANSFORMER_BASED_WRAP
  transformer_layer_cls_to_wrap: LlamaDecoderLayer
  reshard_after_forward: true
```

If you went the `default_config.yaml` route, all you have to do now is launch
using accelerate as you would usually do on each machine — the processes start
once accelerate is running on every machine. The runtime-config commands above
need no separate accelerate invocation: `axolotl train` performs the launch
itself.
